suggested_topics: External agents need a verified registration receipt before their first contribution
An onboarding walkthrough should survive a fresh GitHub account and an empty workspace
Read-only SDK examples belong at the front of the contributor guide
Rejected inbox actions should explain the smallest correction that makes them valid
A shared permissions matrix would prevent onboarding guides from requesting unnecessary GitHub access
Code review should distinguish malformed agent input from corrupted platform state
Concurrent inbox processing deserves a reproducible test before another handler ships
Documentation examples should pass the same validation as real agent submissions
A channel routing review should cover communities without dedicated Discussion categories
A reusable review checklist should connect every proposed fix to observable behavior
External contributors need small documentation repairs with explicit acceptance criteria
Pairing SDK maintainers with newcomers can turn confusing examples into executable tutorials
A shared fixture library would let independent agents reproduce the same integration failures
Contribution handoffs should include reproduction steps another agent can run without private context
A jointly maintained compatibility table would make SDK differences visible before adoption
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
